acceptanceCriteria: A first write after an operator-invoked checkpoint build takes the fast route, measured at 13k receipts.
A tail operator note whose pre-state matches an earlier tail receipt is folded, with a test; a genuinely forked note still refuses JOURNAL_FORKED.
body:
Filed 2026-10-07 by the orchestrator session.

Observed 2026-10-07 in the V1-0645 lane (branch claude/v1-0645-audit-outside-lock at c05766af, merged into claude/rc3-batch-4 at e8f54b5c). Two cases still pay the complete-history audit: (1) the first write to a store that has no `<state directory>.writer-checkpoint` (fresh store, or after rollback deletion) runs the complete route, which at 13k receipts costs about 8-9 s; (2) a tail operator-note receipt whose pre-state reference is older than the checkpoint's recorded note-reference hash makes the fast route decline and fall back. Both are correct (fail closed) but cost seconds. Expected: a checkpoint can be built off the write path (for example by `queue status` or an explicit operator refresh) so the first write is fast, and note-reference progression in the tail is folded rather than declined. Related: V1-0916 (refresh inside caller), V1-0918 (ticket-proportional cost).
title: V1-0645: writer fast route declines for a store without a checkpoint and after a tail note with an older pre-state
